spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is included deliberately so that **stopping is a first-class action**
spec_features.evidence: submit tool dispatched in agent_loop.py:_dispatch (`if name == 'submit': return ws.submit(...)`), which sets ws.submitted=True in sandbox.py:submit(). Loop honors it as a stop: agent_loop.py:104-109 `if ws.submitted and turn >= min_turns...: stop_reason='agent_submitted'; break` and the early branch `if ws.submitted: stop_reason='agent_submitted_early'; break`.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, sets flag, and the flag breaks the loop. A genuine first-class stop action.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly permits `submit`-and-stop (so giving up is legitimate, not coerced)
spec_features.evidence: System prompt delivered to the subject (prompts.py:SYSTEM_PROMPT) states: 'If you conclude you cannot complete the task, you may also call `submit` explaining why and stop.' This text is actually built into SYSTEM_PROMPT and sent as Message(role=SYSTEM) in agent_loop.py:run_episode; its referenced submit tool is fully implemented and honored (see above).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND the referenced tool is fully built/dispatched/honored. Same underlying mechanism as the prior item.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: "so 'giving up gracefully' is an available action and not something we force" — framed to distinguish give-up from spiral for the measurement

spec_features.evidence: max_turns read from config (config.py:from_dict max_turns=exp['max_turns']; experiment.yaml:19 max_turns: 25), passed to run_episode (run_experiment.py:63), and enforced by `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` with `else: result.stop_reason = 'max_turns'` (agent_loop.py:65, 114-115). The loop terminates when the budget is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: A real enforced hard cap that bounds the number of failure turns the subject experiences.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:104-106 `if ws.submitted and turn >= min_turns_before_early_stop: result.stop_reason = 'agent_submitted'; break` — the submit flag is checked and breaks the loop, with a gating min-turns threshold (min_turns_before_early_stop default 6) read from config.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a clean stop; early submits recorded separately as agent_submitted_early (still breaks the loop). Same submit mechanism, with the min-turns gate added.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: "# Model produced only text with no action for a while -> stalled." and min_turns gating exists "so we always capture some trajectory" (per structure: early stops still break but are labeled differently for analysis)
